To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrated the long-term efficacy of a low-dose systemic treatment with AONs adsorbed onto nanoparticles.

we demonstrated that a low dose of 2′O-methyl-phosporothioate antisenses, adsorbed onto nanoparticles, provokes widespread and long-lasting dystrophin restoration in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystropy.

dystrophin restoration can be measured 90 days after intraperitonially administered ZM2-AO NPs complexes, and the percentage and intensity of dystrophin positive fibres and exon 23 skipping are higher in ZM2-Ao NPs complexes treated mice in comparison with naked AON treated mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic approach for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystropy, which is based on the use of naked 2′OMEPs-AONs complexed with ZM2 nanoparticles.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) by the use of antisense oligonucleotides.
the development of a new generation of antisense oligonucleotides, the so-called 2′-OMePS AOs, and with the use of nanoparticles (NPs) as a delivery system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ZM2 nanoparticles and AONs represents an effective therapeutic strategy for Duchenne muscular dystrophies.

the dystrophin protein is still present in the skeletal muscles 90 days after the end of the low-dose treatment, and that the level of dystrophin restoration is still significant, even if lower, compared to 7 days after treatment.

, in the mdx mouse, the ZM2 NP-2′OMe PS AON complex is able to induce long-lasting exon 23 skipping, dystrophin expression and functional improvement, even after a single 3-week intraperitoneal administration of 7.5 mg/Kg/week.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of ZM2 nanoparticles with AONs is a very promising strategy for the systemic treatment of DMD.
we have developed a systemic exon-skipping therapy that can be used to restore dystrophin in mdx mice for at least 90 days after a course of intraperitoneally administered ZM2 NP AONs.

we have demonstrated that low doses of 2′OMeoPS AONs adsorbed onto nanoparticles are able to restore dystrophin protein expression in the skeletal muscles and heart of mdx mice, and that the dystrophin protein restoration persists for 90 days.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dystrophin restoration we observed in the skeletal muscles 7 days following the end of a low-dose intraperitoneal administration was still measurable 3 months later.

a single course of treatment with a low dose of 2′O-methyl-phosphate-sulfur antisense oligonucleotides adsorbed on ZM2 nanoparticles can lead to persistent restoration of dystrophin protein and exon-skipping in the muscles of mdx dystrophic mice for at least 3 months after the end of the treatment.

a low dose of 2′OMEP AON and Z2 NP-AON complexes administered intraperitoneally to dystrophic mdx mice for 4 weeks is able to maintain dystrophin expression in the muscles for 90 days after the end of treatment, thus providing a proof of concept for the development of a chronic exon-skipping therapy in DMD patients.
